findings.passage: Capping state spending and capping the rate of government spending growth; passing term limits for politicians, ending taxpayer-funded pensions, and enacting a gift ban; deregulating to attract businesses to Pennsylvania; ensuring education funding follows students rather than systems; requiring voter ID and repealing universal mail-in voting; and protecting constitutional rights and pro-life values with common-sense exemptions.
findings.note: Key Issues field of his 2026 Bucks County Beacon candidate profile (candidate-supplied). Lists requiring voter ID and repealing universal mail-in voting among his priorities. Page date not shown; 2026 cycle.

findings.passage: “The integrity of our elections is critically important. People deserve to be confident in the fairness of the process, and as a member of the board, I want people to be motivated to vote because of that confidence,” Coleman said. “We’ve seen that our elections could be improved, and I look forward to spending more time considering possible changes.”
findings.note: Statement in his official release on reappointment to the state Election Law Advisory Board. General election-integrity statement; names no ID rule.

findings.passage: “I’m focused on ensuring that our election equipment is adequately tested prior to elections and will be reintroducing legislation next session to accomplish that goal. The Election Law Advisory Board is a great resource to find other opportunities for improvement,” Coleman said.
findings.note: Same release. He names election equipment testing as his focus. Related topic, not an ID rule.

His official accomplishments page lists SB 1 (2023-24 session) as co-sponsored with Sen. Laughlin, status passed Senate with no House passage, described as a joint resolution mandating voter identification through a constitutional amendment.

findings.motion: Senate: Third consideration and final passage (PN 26)

findings.motion: co sponsor, PN 385 (House reported, passed House May 22, 2023). PN 26 (passed Senate Jan 11, 2023) also read; the voter ID paragraph reads the same in both.
